title: Rosa sets about the harvest (paraphrase C)
topic: A farmer named Rosa brings in the wheat harvest: the combine cuts the field, sacks of grain go onto a trailer, clouds gather, the family works until evening, Rosa closes the gate
tail_E: A week later the mill turns the new grain into fine white
target_note: Same target as formulations A and B: 'flour' is predictable only from the harvest context (wheat, grain, sacks, a mill); 'turns the new grain into fine white' is completed by flour. The word does not occur in the units or the tail, and neither does its German equivalent 'Mehl'. ' flour' is a single Pythia token (id 12274). Pilot check with pythia-160m (tail selection only): p(' flour') = 0.22 on the all-English rendering, rank 1 (next: ' wheat' 0.06); still rank 1 (p = 0.14) on the K=8 C3 rendering.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (DEV04C, farmer Rosa, paraphrase C, development family)
notes: Formulation C: third independent re-phrasing of the ten DEV04A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Rosa, wording different from A and B). Replacements include sets about the harvest at dawn (macht sich an die Ernte im Morgengrauen), tall wheat ripples gently in the light wind (hoher Weizen kräuselt sich sanft im leichten Wind), manoeuvres the combine over the field (manövriert den Mähdrescher über den Acker), big machine severs the stalks in long strips (große Maschine kappt die Halme in langen Streifen), stuffs the grain into big sacks (stopft das Korn in große Säcke), workers hoist the sacks onto a wagon (Arbeiter hieven die Säcke auf einen Karren), old tractor takes the wagon to the farmstead (alter Traktor bringt den Karren zum Gehöft), heavy clouds build up over the hilltops (schwere Wolken ballen sich über den Hügelkuppen), the family stays at work until late evening (die Familie bleibt bei der Arbeit bis zum späten Abend), locks the gate after a whole day's work (verschließt das Tor nach einem ganzen Tag Arbeit). Units 2 and 8 use reflexive verbs (kräuselt sich, ballen sich); no separable verbs. Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Development family: used for dose/threshold choice only.
